text:
Maria Chen: Quick FYI — finished the per-model perf sweep across Llama/Mistral/Mixtral/Qwen for the new kernel-selector heuristics. Found a reproducible drop for Qwen-14B and Mixtral-7B at mid batch sizes (4-8). Dumping the short notes + profiler snippets here.

perf-bot: sweep finished: artifacts at https://perf.redwood/sweeps/1932104321 :thumbsup:

Sanjay Patel: Interesting. Can you paste the failing sample from the perf harness?

Maria Chen: Pasted below — this is the canonical failure case (ctx=8192, batch=8). Notice kernel fallback and kv evict spikes.

```
perf-bench: qwen-14b @ ctx=8192, batch=8
throughput: 820 tokens/s (baseline 1100)
latency p50: 95ms p95: 320ms
kernel_selected: generic_attention (fallback)
kv_evictions_per_s: 35
notes: sudden spike in copy/transpose time in attention kernel
```

Olivia Nguyen: That fallback + evict smell like RoPE scaling + KV layout mismatch. We saw earlier that Qwen's head_dim -> kv packing interacts poorly with flash-attn heuristics.

Luca Romano: Also check batch boundary padding — our dynamic-batcher was producing slightly different seq lengths distribution for batch=8, so per-request kernel choice became inconsistent. Could cause extra memcpy.

Kai Park: I ran a quick trace on Mixtral-7B one-hour ago:

```
trace: mixtral-7b / batch=6 / ctx=4096
kernel: mixed paths: flash_attn -> fallback_generic
copy_time_ms: 14.2
attn_compute_ms: 38.7
kv_cache_evictions: 12/s (spike when rolling over segments)
rope_scale_factor: 1.15 (enabled)
```

Sanjay Patel: Key suspicion: rope_scale_factor > 1 pushes attention into numeric regime that triggers alternative kernels (we have a threshold that disables flash kernels when rotary factors change). Kernel selector then picks slower path. Coupled with inconsistent batch shapes, that gives regression.

Olivia Nguyen: Proposed quick config to test (force preferred kernel + tighten batch soft limit):

```
{"model": "qwen-14b", "kernel_selector.prefer_flash_attn": true, "kernel_selector.rope_scale_threshold": 0.3, "batcher.batch_soft_limit": 6, "kv_cache.eviction_policy": "lru", "kv_cache.max_segment_age_ms": 120000}
```

Maria Chen: Thanks — will run that. Also planning a run where we disable rope scaling entirely for Qwen to separate variables.

Luca Romano: If disabling rope fixes it, then we should update the per-model kernel hints in the model catalog rather than changing global selector. Qwen seems sensitive.

Kai Park: Another angle — reduce kv segment size to avoid thrash when longctx clients have bursty prefixes. Current default is 64K per segment; try 16K for the test.

Sanjay Patel: Also instrument kernel selection logs to include the decision vector (seq_len, head_dim, rope_scale, batch_actual). Right now we log just kernel name which doesn't help triage.

Maria Chen: Agreed. I'll add verbose selector logs for the next sweep.

perf-bot: scheduled job: sweep-qwen-14b-1932104321-run2 (queued)

Olivia Nguyen: If you need a fast local repro, run the harness with `--seed 42 --prefill 512 --burst 6` and watch `kv_evictions` metric in the dashboard.

Maria Chen: Plan: 1) run with forced flash-attn pref, tighter batch_soft_limit, smaller kv segments; 2) run with rope scaling off; 3) collect kernel-decision logs. I'll post results here. Anyone want to pair on the run?

Luca Romano: I can join for the first run at 3pm PT.

Kai Park: ping me for the trace aggregation script — I'll attach aggregated flamegraphs after the run.

Maria Chen: Great, thanks all. If the pref forced run recovers throughput we'll add a temporary per-model hint. If rope is root cause we'll update quantized-on-serve pipeline to better normalize rotary factors.

Sanjay Patel: One more micro-note — watch out for head_dim*kv_dim mismatches with mixed-precision matmuls; occasional misaligned strides fall back to slower kernels. If you see `stride_mismatch` in logs that's the other culprit.

Maria Chen: Noted. I'll include stride_mismatch in the verbose list. Will report back with numbers. :white_check_mark:
